title: GPS coordinates in transit can be intercepted and linked to child's identity
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted over the network could be intercepted by third parties and linked to the child's identity through metadata or correlation with other data sources.

title: Sharing GPS data inherently identifies child's location
description: The child's device transmits live GPS coordinates, which inherently identifies the child's physical location and movements, enabling identification of the child through location data.

title: GPS data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized third parties during transmission, leading to unauthorized disclosure of location information.

title: Backend may store excessive location data
description: The mobile app backend may store more location data than necessary for the intended purpose, violating data minimization principles by retaining historical GPS records beyond what is required.

title: GPS data may be used for unauthorized purposes
description: The mobile app backend may use the collected GPS data for purposes beyond what was intended by the child or their guardians, such as behavioral profiling or third-party sharing.

title: Location data in transit exposed to interception
description: Location pings containing personal location data are transmitted between backend and geofencing engine. Data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing user location information.

title: Location metadata enables user tracking and linking
description: Location data in transit contains metadata (timestamps, device identifiers) that could be used to link the user's movements to other data sources or track user behavior patterns across sessions.

title: Geofencing engine processes location data beyond intended scope
description: The geofencing engine receives and processes location data that may be stored, logged, or used for purposes beyond the immediate zone-checking function, potentially violating minimality principle.

title: Backend shares identifiable location data with internal process
description: The backend forwards location pings that contain personally identifiable information (user location) to another system component, creating identification risk through data sharing.

title: Linkability of Zone Definitions to Family Members
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) stored in the Family Account Store could be linked across different contexts to identify family members' locations and movement patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routines and associations.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain address or location data that can be correlated with family member identities

title: Identifiability via Location Data
description: Addresses or location data in zone definitions could directly identify family members, their home addresses, school locations, and frequent visitation patterns to friends' houses, creating a detailed profile of their movements.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain specific location data that can be used to identify individuals

title: Usurpation of Location Data for Unintended Purposes
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine may use the zone definitions and location data for purposes beyond geofencing, such as behavioral profiling, targeted advertising, or sharing with third parties without explicit consent.
assumptions: The process has access to broader data usage capabilities beyond its stated geofencing function

title: Disclosure of Location Data to Unauthorized Parties
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine may expose location data or zone definitions to unauthorized internal or external parties through improper access controls, logging, or data sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Access controls or data handling procedures at the destination process are insufficient

title: Metadata-Based Linkability in Transit
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, data sizes, access patterns) could be used to link or identify family members' activities and locations even if the actual zone definitions are encrypted or anonymized.
assumptions: Metadata is not properly protected during data transmission
uncertainty_note: Metadata threats are less common but possible depending on network monitoring capabilities

title: Location-based Linkability via Geofencing Notifications
description: The geofencing engine shares arrival/departure notifications that inherently contain location context, enabling linkage of an individual's movements across different zones and time periods. This creates a trail of location-based activities that can be correlated to build a movement profile.

title: Location Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Geofencing notifications transmitted between the geofencing engine and parent system may be intercepted or logged during transmission, exposing location-based movement data to unauthorized parties or systems.

title: Location Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The parent system receives and processes location-based notifications that may be stored, indexed, or shared in ways that expose sensitive movement patterns beyond the intended scope of the geofencing functionality.

title: Identification of Parent and Child at Registration
description: The parent provides highly identifiable personal information (name, DOB, school) about themselves and their child during account registration. This act of sharing creates a direct identification threat as the data inherently identifies specific individuals.

title: Linkability of Data in Transit
description: Data transmitted from the parent to the mobile app backend could be intercepted or observed, enabling linkage of the parent-child relationship and geofence zone definitions to specific individuals through metadata or traffic analysis.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Profile Data
description: The mobile app backend may store or process the child's profile information (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones in a manner that exposes this sensitive data to unauthorized parties or systems.

title: Excessive Data Collection and Storage
description: The process may retain more personal data than necessary for the stated purpose of account registration and geofence management, including the child's school information which may not be essential for core functionality.

title: Unauthorized Use of Child Profile Data
description: The mobile app backend may use the collected child profile data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) for purposes beyond the stated registration and geofence management, such as third-party sharing or profiling.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure via Family Account & Permissions Store
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) receives and stores sensitive personal data including account information, child profiles, and geofence zone data. If the data store lacks proper access controls, encryption, or retention policies, this could lead to unintended disclosure of personal data to unauthorized parties or through data breaches.
assumptions: The data store may not have adequate security controls or may retain data longer than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a general data disclosure node; specific tree node may vary based on full LINDDUN Pro threat tree.

title: Linkability of Stored Personal Data
description: The data flow from Backend to DataStore involves account, child profile, and geofence zone data that could be linked across different contexts or with other data sources. Metadata or derived information from this flow could enable linking of individuals to their family relationships or location patterns.
assumptions: The data contains identifiers or quasi-identifiers that could be used for linkage.
uncertainty_note: Linkability threat depends on the specific data fields and their combination potential.

title: Excessive Data Collection by Backend
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) may collect and share more personal data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose (storing account, child profile, and geofence zone data). This violates the minimality principle of data protection.
assumptions: The backend may not implement data minimization principles during data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the backend's data collection practices may not be minimal.

title: Location data in transit could identify child's movements
description: Location data transmitted from parent to backend could be intercepted, revealing the child's current location or movement patterns, potentially identifying the child's whereabouts to unauthorized parties.

title: Location data could be linked to identify child
description: Location data in transit could be correlated with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps) to uniquely identify the child and their movements, creating a linkable profile.

title: Backend could disclose child's location to unauthorized parties
description: The mobile app backend (P1) could store or process the child's location data in a way that allows disclosure to unauthorized parties, such as through improper access controls or data sharing.

title: Backend may store excessive location data
description: The backend may retain location history longer or with more precision than necessary for the stated purpose of viewing current location, violating data minimization principles.

title: Backend may allow unauthorized access to location data
description: The backend may have insufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized users or systems to access the child's location data.

title: Location History Data in Transit is Identifiable
description: Location history data transmitted from the Location History Store to the Mobile App Backend contains inherently identifiable information about individuals' movements and patterns. The data in transit can be used to identify specific users and their whereabouts.

title: Location History Data Can Be Linked with Other Data Sources
description: Location history data transmitted in this flow can potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps, app usage data) to create detailed user profiles and track movement patterns across different contexts.

title: Location History Data May Be Improperly Disclosed at Destination
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives sensitive location history data. If the backend does not implement adequate access controls and data protection measures, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized internal or external parties.

title: Location Data Handling May Violate Privacy Regulations
description: Location history is classified as sensitive personal data under regulations like GDPR. The Mobile App Backend must comply with strict requirements for collection, storage, and processing of location data, including obtaining proper consent and implementing data minimization principles.

title: Child location data shared by parent identifies child's whereabouts
description: When the parent (EE1) shares the child's location data with the system, the act of sharing itself exposes the child's real-time location, making the child identifiable through their location patterns and movements.
assumptions: Parent is authorized to share child's location; system accepts and processes this data

title: Parent's sharing action links child location to parent identity
description: The parent's act of initiating the location sharing creates a link between the child's location data and the parent's identity, enabling correlation of child movements with parent activities.
assumptions: System can associate the sharing action with the parent's account

title: Metadata in transit enables linking of parent and child locations
description: Metadata accompanying the location data in transit (e.g., source/destination identifiers, timestamps) can be used to link the parent's identity with the child's location, creating a privacy risk even if content is encrypted.
assumptions: Metadata is transmitted alongside the location data

title: Location data in transit can be intercepted to identify child's whereabouts
description: Location data transmitted between parent and backend is vulnerable to interception, allowing unauthorized parties to identify the child's real-time location and movement patterns.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully secured; interception is possible

title: Backend may disclose child location to unauthorized parties
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives and stores the child's location data, creating a risk that this sensitive data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls or data breaches.
assumptions: Backend has access to stored location data; access controls may be insufficient

title: Backend processes location data to identify child's patterns and routines
description: The backend processes the child's location data, potentially building profiles of the child's movement patterns, routines, and habits, which could be used to identify the child beyond the immediate location sharing purpose.
assumptions: Backend performs data processing and storage; profiling capabilities exist

title: Location data linkability during transmission
description: Child's live location data transmitted in transit could be intercepted and linked with other data sources to reconstruct movement patterns and identify the child's routine locations.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data
description: Secondary guardian (EE3) may disclose or share the child's live location data with unauthorized third parties beyond the intended scope of access.

title: Usurpation of location data for unauthorized purposes
description: Secondary guardian may use the child's live location data for purposes beyond the authorized scope, such as surveillance, stalking, or other unauthorized monitoring activities.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in data sharing
description: Sharing live location data with a secondary guardian may violate child privacy regulations or consent requirements, particularly if proper authorization or age-appropriate consent mechanisms are not in place.

title: Unauthorized Use of Analytics Data
description: Advertising/analytics partner may use the aggregated usage and engagement analytics beyond the agreed scope (e.g., for profiling, selling to third parties, or building user profiles), violating the intended purpose of funding the app's free tier.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Data
description: Even aggregated analytics data could potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., device IDs, IP addresses, or other metadata) to re-identify individual users, especially if the aggregation is not sufficiently coarse-grained.

title: Data Leakage to Third Parties
description: The advertising/analytics partner may share or leak the received analytics data to unauthorized third parties, violating data minimization and purpose limitation principles.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Data Sharing
description: Sharing aggregated user analytics with external partners may violate GDPR or other privacy regulations if proper consent mechanisms, data minimization, and transparency requirements are not met.

title: Location data linkability in transit
description: Location data transmitted in the check-in/SOS message can be used to link the child to specific geographic locations and times, potentially enabling tracking patterns.

title: Location data identification during transmission
description: Location metadata in the message can identify the child's current whereabouts, revealing sensitive personal information about their movements.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: Location data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, compromising the child's privacy and safety.

title: Location data disclosure at destination
description: The parent (destination) may disclose the child's location data to third parties or use it beyond the intended purpose.

title: Attributable SOS message at destination
description: The SOS message can be attributed to the child, creating a record that links the child to the emergency situation.
